name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
short: In a review of 41 reports in chronic lung disease, stomach and bowel symptoms occurred but were no more common than in control groups, including at higher doses.
text: A review of 41 articles in which N-acetylcysteine was used at 600 mg/day or more (up to 3000 mg/day), mostly by mouth in people with chronic respiratory diseases, found that the safety profile was similar at high and standard doses; gastrointestinal symptoms were reported but were no more common than in the control group. In a network meta-analysis of 7 randomised trials in 2753 people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, adverse events with N-acetylcysteine and two related medicines were mild and generally well tolerated. These data come from people with chronic lung disease. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
